honorific: Forms of address, register and fidelity guidance (zh→en): render imperial, noble, official, clerical and humble self-references naturally by speaker role and register (for example, imperial 孤/朕/寡人 as 'I' or majestic 'we', never literally 'the lone one'; courtier 臣 as 'Your servant' or 'Your subject'), avoiding awkward repetition. Grade forms of address (大人, 殿下, 公子, 先生, 师父, 长老, etc.) consistently by speaker-to-listener hierarchy and setting, never producing ungrammatical calques such as 'the sir'. Avoid stiff Chinese calques: drop demonstrative 'That' before a named character (那<Name> -> '<Name>'), never insert unrequested parenthetical glosses into narration, and match singular vs. plural to the characters present. Preserve source logic faithfully across multi-clause sentences—negation scope, correlative conditionals, delayed realizations, exact numbers and quantifier polarity, agent/object direction, and kinship seniority. Translate idioms (成语) and allusions by their contextual meaning rather than surface words, and format embedded poems and lyrics with explicit line breaks (\n).
